title: 0xc000007b was a BCD object type error, not a corrupt kernel
body: The MELLI entry {b7173bfb} was typed 'Real-mode Boot Sector' with path \EFI\MELLI\vmlinuz.efi. That legacy type cannot start an EFI PE image, so every attempt produced 0xc000007b and the stub itself was fine all along (14758912 B, sha E73DC060). bcdedit also cannot create the correct 'Firmware Application (101fffff)' type, so this entry had no repair path at all: it could only be deleted, and the stub reached through GRUB instead.

title: Default bcdedit /enum shows 2 objects out of 21
body: bcdedit /enum renders only the bootmgr-reachable chain, which on this box was {bootmgr} plus {current}. The full store is 21 objects. A bogus firmware entry therefore is invisible in the default view and invisible in the F12 menu (it was absent from fwbootmgr displayorder), yet present on disk. Use bcdedit /enum all, bcdedit /enum firmware, and reg query HKLM\BCD00000000\Objects before asserting anything is absent.

title: Deletion proven on four independent surfaces at once
body: Object removal was confirmed by targeted lookup ('There are no matching objects'), whole-store /enum all (21 identifiers, zero matches for the guid, MELLI, vmlinuz, real-mode), raw export byte search (32768 B export, UTF-16LE hits 0 for MELLI/vmlinuz/hyper-edge/guid), and the live hive (HKLM\BCD00000000\Objects 21 keys, MATCH=0). Neighbouring guids b7173bed/bee/bef/bf0 survived, which proves a surgical delete rather than a store reset.

title: A second shim entry hid under a network-card description
body: {b7173bfa} pointed at the same \EFI\ubuntu\shimx64.efi as the working {0f7b2723} 'Ubuntu' entry but was described 'UEFI: HTTP IPv4 Network Card' and was not in fwbootmgr displayorder. Two Firmware Application objects targeting one file is the tell. It was deleted after exporting the store to a 32768 B backup; counts went 21 to 20 objects and 9 to 8 firmware identifiers, and the before/after diff was exactly the seven-line block.

title: Elevated bcdedit needs -File; inline -Command mangled the guid
body: Two delete attempts through Start-Process -Verb RunAs -ArgumentList '-Command bcdedit /delete "{guid}" /f' returned 'The delete command specified is not valid', which reads like a store lock but was nested-quote mangling. The same delete through '-File script.ps1' with the guid in single quotes succeeded first try. When an elevated verb reports a syntax class error, suspect the quoting before suspecting the object.

title: A literal $env:TEMP made the elevated child a silent no-op
body: Because $env:TEMP sat inside single quotes in -ArgumentList, the child received the literal text and ran nothing, and Start-Process still returned exit 0. That read as success until no output file appeared. Pass absolute paths into -ArgumentList, never a variable, and verify an elevated child by the artifact it writes rather than by the launcher's exit code.

title: An elevated child cannot be inspected from a non-admin parent
body: tasklist and Get-CimInstance run non-elevated show the elevated PowerShell with an empty CommandLine, so a hung elevated script cannot be identified by its arguments, only by PID. Verification must go through the file the child was told to write. This is also why a looping elevated script that was doubling a file looked like two anonymous processes.

title: cat f >> f doubled a BCD dump to 257 MB on a 98%-full disk
body: A debugging line intended to show output appended the file to itself inside an elevated loop, growing 174 MB to 220 MB to 257 MB while it ran. It had to be killed from another elevated shell and the file deleted. Never use 'cat FILE >> FILE'; use Get-Content/type, and treat any unexplained fast-growing file as a live writer to be stopped before it is read.

title: '> file -Append' truncates: a reg load error erased its own log
body: Writing 'reg load HKLM\X $hive > $out -Append 2>&1' is not an append; the redirection truncates and the trailing -Append is a stray argument. The first line of the report (HIVE_BYTES) vanished and the log opened with the error instead. Use Out-File -Append or Tee-Object for anything that must accumulate across commands.

title: Cleanup deleted a tracked project script
body: rm -f of a temp-named script matched a real repository file esp_check.ps1, the change-triggered ESP validator, because the same name was chosen for a throwaway. It was restored with git checkout -- esp_check.ps1 from HEAD and git status returned clean for that path. Before deleting in a repo, run git ls-files on the name; prefer a temp directory for scratch scripts.

title: A guid regex anchored to the line reported 0 objects where 21 existed
body: reg query HKLM\BCD00000000\Objects prints full key paths, so '^\{guid\}$' matched nothing and the report read LIVE_OBJECTS=0 while the previous pass had counted 21. A zero produced by a parser that does not match the instrument's output format is a measurement bug, never evidence of absence, and it fails in the direction that looks like a finding.

title: probe_melli.ps1 reports PARTUUID drift against a matching GUID
body: The probe prints 'FAIL: P4 PARTUUID drifted' on a line that simultaneously prints guid={e4ff9384-c2c7-4605-bbe4-361d20f099fe}, which is exactly the expected value. The comparison is wrong, not the partition table. This is the RULE 0S failure mode: read the cited line before accepting an instrument's verdict, because it is often right about a thing and wrong about which.

title: GRUB chainloader of a kernel EFI stub passes no cmdline and no initramfs
body: The MELLI menuentry does 'chainloader /EFI/MELLI/vmlinuz.efi' against a 14.7 MB kernel with no initrd beside it, so it would boot with an empty command line and no root=. MELLI_OS/INSTALL_191G.md step 3 requires placing the initramfs, and the correct entry is 'linuxefi ... root=PARTUUID=<new> ro' plus 'initrdefi .../initrd.img'. Secure Boot is Off, so signature enforcement is not the blocker; the missing cmdline is.

title: CORRECTS chainloader-passes-no-initrd: chainloader is right, NVMe was the gap
body: The earlier row claiming the GRUB entry needs linuxefi+initrdefi was wrong. arch/x86/Kconfig in the 7.0.14 tree proves it: with CMDLINE_BOOL=y and CMDLINE_OVERRIDE unset, the built-in 'root=PARTUUID=e4ff9384-... rw console=tty0 console=ttyS0,115200' applies whenever the loader passes nothing, and GRUB chainloader passes nothing (CMDLINE_FORCE does not even exist on x86, so worker2's scripts/config --enable of it was a silent no-op). No initramfs is needed either: EXT4_FS=y, DEVTMPFS=y, AHCI=y and EFI_STUB=y are all built in. The single missing piece is storage: '# CONFIG_BLK_DEV_NVME is not set'. On the NVMe-only Disk0 (WD PC SN5000S) the kernel cannot see any block device, so the current ESP kernel would VFS-panic. Fix: enable CONFIG_BLK_DEV_NVME (+NVME_CORE via select), rebuild, QEMU-test, redeploy to ESP. GRUB chainloader entry itself stays as-is.

title: QEMU -nographic dies stopped in detached tmux: SIGTTIN on terminal stdio
body: QEMU take1 in detached tmux showed 0 CPU + 0 serial bytes: /proc state T (stopped), wchan do_signal_stop, stdin=/dev/pts. -nographic reads the terminal; with no attached client the read stops the process via SIGTTIN. Fix used for all later takes: -display none -monitor none -serial file:SER with stdin from /dev/null. Diagnose any silent black-box VM the same way: state T + do_signal_stop means job control stopped it, not that the guest is slow.

title: QEMU pre-flight GREEN: NVMe kernel mounts golden rootfs to MELLI-OS banner
body: NVMe kernel 5d75b9a6 (BLK_DEV_NVME=y) vs golden image melli-full-205G.img on emulated nvme: nvme0 probed (pci 0000:00:04.0), nvme0n1 201049088 blocks, EXT4 mounted UUID ef7586d7 ro, VFS Mounted root device 259:0, Run /sbin/init, rcS ran python 3.16.0a1 gil_enabled False and printed MELLI-OS 1.0 (hyper-edge), then login prompt. Two harness-only failures on the way: root=UUID= cannot resolve on the partitionless test image (use root=/dev/nvme0n1 there; real disk has GPT so baked PARTUUID applies), and root=rw on readonly=on backing fails superblock write (use ro; rcS remount,rw error is expected and non-fatal). Serial log /srv/mb/qemu-serial.log.

title: ESP kernel replaced with NVMe build, hash-proven, old kept as .bak
body: deploy_melli_kernel.ps1 (self-elevating, one UAC) mounted ESP Volume 80ce903d, refused paths it did not find, backed live kernel to vmlinuz.efi.bak-20261113-163007 (14758912 B e73dc060, the no-NVMe build), wrote vmlinuz-melli-7.0.14-nvme (14824448 B 5d75b9a6), read back same sha+size, unmounted S:. GRUB chainloader entry unchanged and still valid. esp_check scope is only EFI/ubuntu/grub.cfg which no step wrote, so no re-run needed. Next: bare-metal boot via GRUB menu MELLI-OS 1.0 entry; firmware boot order untouched (Windows first) so a failure costs one reboot.
